licenses.slogans: decl slogans are currently ABSENT by policy: theorem_matching.csv's formal_slogan is license-contested upstream (CC-BY-SA card vs CC-BY-NC-SA paper, BRAIN.md:452) so it stays link-facts-only, and slogan.csv (CC-BY-4.0) turned out to cover informal statements exclusively (0/2.57M rows reference a formal id). label: FirstOrder.Language
docstring:
A first-order language consists of a type of functions of every natural-number arity and a
type of relations of every natural-number arity.

label: FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormula
docstring:
`BoundedFormula α n` is the type of formulas with free variables indexed by `α` and `n` in-scope
bound variables indexed by `Fin n`.
code:
inductive BoundedFormula : ℕ → Type max u v u'
  | falsum {n} : BoundedFormula n
  | equal {n} (t₁ t₂ : L.Term (α ⊕ (Fin n))) : BoundedFormula n
  | rel {n l : ℕ} (R : L.Relations l) (ts : Fin l → L.Term (α ⊕ (Fin n))) : BoundedFormula n
  /-- The implication between two bounded formulas. -/
  | imp {n} (f₁ f₂ : BoundedFormula n) : BoundedFormula n
  /-- The universal quantifier over bounded formulas. -/
  | all {n} (f : BoundedFormula (n + 1)) : BoundedFormula n

label: FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormula.IsAtomic
docstring:
An atomic formula is either equality or a relation symbol applied to terms.
Note that `⊥` and `⊤` are not considered atomic in this convention.
code:
inductive IsAtomic : L.BoundedFormula α n → Prop
  | equal (t₁ t₂ : L.Term (α ⊕ (Fin n))) : IsAtomic (t₁.bdEqual t₂)
  | rel {l : ℕ} (R : L.Relations l) (ts : Fin l → L.Term (α ⊕ (Fin n))) :
    IsAtomic (R.boundedFormula ts)

label: FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormula.IsPrenex
docstring:
Indicates that a bounded formula is in prenex normal form - that is, it consists of quantifiers
applied to a quantifier-free formula.
code:
inductive IsPrenex : ∀ {n}, L.BoundedFormula α n → Prop
  | of_isQF {n : ℕ} {φ : L.BoundedFormula α n} (h : IsQF φ) : IsPrenex φ
  | all {n : ℕ} {φ : L.BoundedFormula α (n + 1)} (h : IsPrenex φ) : IsPrenex φ.all
  | ex {n : ℕ} {φ : L.BoundedFormula α (n + 1)} (h : IsPrenex φ) : IsPrenex φ.ex

label: FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormula.IsQF
docstring:
A quantifier-free formula is a formula defined without quantifiers. These are all equivalent
to Boolean combinations of atomic formulas.
code:
inductive IsQF : L.BoundedFormula α n → Prop
  | falsum : IsQF falsum
  | of_isAtomic {φ :  L.BoundedFormula α n} (h : IsAtomic φ) : IsQF φ
  | imp {φ₁ φ₂ :  L.BoundedFormula α n} (h₁ : IsQF φ₁) (h₂ : IsQF φ₂) : IsQF (φ₁.imp φ₂)

label: FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormula.Realize
docstring:
A bounded formula can be evaluated as true or false by giving values to each free and bound
variable.
code:
def Realize : ∀ {l} (_f : L.BoundedFormula α l) (_v : α → M) (_xs : Fin l → M), Prop
  | _, falsum, _v, _xs => False
  | _, equal t₁ t₂, v, xs => t₁.realize (Sum.elim v xs) = t₂.realize (Sum.elim v xs)
  | _, rel R ts, v, xs => RelMap R fun i => (ts i).realize (Sum.elim v xs)
  | _, imp f₁ f₂, v, xs => Realize f₁ v xs → Realize f₂ v xs
  | _, all f, v, xs => ∀ x : M, Realize f v (snoc xs x)

  | _, falsum, _v, _xs => False
  | _, equal t₁ t₂, v, xs => t₁.realize (Sum.elim v xs) = t₂.realize (Sum.elim v xs)
  | _, rel R ts, v, xs => RelMap R fun i => (ts i).realize (Sum.elim v xs)
  | _, imp f₁ f₂, v, xs => Realize f₁ v xs → Realize f₂ v xs
  | _, all f, v, xs => ∀ x : M, Realize f v (snoc xs x)

label: FirstOrder.Language.exists_elementaryEmbedding_card_eq
docstring:

and an infinite `L`-structure `M`, then there is an elementary embedding in the appropriate
direction between then `M` and a structure of cardinality `κ`.

    (κ : Cardinal.{w}) (h1 : ℵ₀ ≤ κ) (h2 : lift.{w} L.card ≤ Cardinal.lift.{max u v} κ) :
    ∃ N : Bundled L.Structure, (Nonempty (N ↪ₑ[L] M) ∨ Nonempty (M ↪ₑ[L] N)) ∧ #N = κ := by

label: FirstOrder.Language.exists_elementarySubstructure_card_eq
docstring:
The **Downward Löwenheim–Skolem theorem** :
If `s` is a set in an `L`-structure `M` and `κ` an infinite cardinal such that
`max (#s, L.card) ≤ κ` and `κ ≤ # M`, then `M` has an elementary substructure containing `s` of
cardinality `κ`.

    (h2 : Cardinal.lift.{w'} #s ≤ Cardinal.lift.{w} κ)
    (h3 : Cardinal.lift.{w'} L.card ≤ Cardinal.lift.{max u v} κ)
    (h4 : Cardinal.lift.{w} κ ≤ Cardinal.lift.{w'} #M) :
    ∃ S : L.ElementarySubstructure M, s ⊆ S ∧ Cardinal.lift.{w'} #S = Cardinal.lift.{w} κ := by

docstring:
Prop structure holding the assumptions of the Picard-Lindelöf theorem.
`IsPicardLindelof f t₀ x₀ a r L K`, where `t₀ ∈ Icc tmin tmax`, means that the time-dependent vector
field `f` satisfies the conditions to admit an integral curve `α : ℝ → E` to `f` defined on
`Icc tmin tmax`

structure IsPicardLindelof {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    (f : ℝ → E → E) {tmin tmax : ℝ} (t₀ : Icc tmin tmax) (x₀ : E) (a r L K : ℝ≥0) : Prop where

label: IsPicardLindelof.exists_eq_forall_mem_Icc_eq_picard
docstring:
**Picard-Lindelöf (Cauchy-Lipschitz) theorem**, integral form. This version shows the existence
of a local solution whose initial point `x` may be different from the centre `x₀` of the closed
ball within which the properties of the vector field hold.
code:
theorem exists_eq_forall_mem_Icc_eq_picard
    (hf : IsPicardLindelof f t₀ x₀ a r L K) (hx : x ∈ closedBall x₀ r) :
    ∃ α : ℝ → E, α t₀ = x ∧ ∀ t ∈ Icc tmin tmax, α t = ODE.picard f t₀ x α t := by

label: IsPicardLindelof.exists_eq_forall_mem_Icc_hasDerivWithinAt
docstring:
**Picard-Lindelöf (Cauchy-Lipschitz) theorem**, differential form. This version shows the
existence of a local solution whose initial point `x` may be different from the centre `x₀` of
the closed ball within which the properties of the vector field hold.
code:
theorem exists_eq_forall_mem_Icc_hasDerivWithinAt
    (hf : IsPicardLindelof f t₀ x₀ a r L K) (hx : x ∈ closedBall x₀ r) :
    ∃ α : ℝ → E, α t₀ = x ∧
      ∀ t ∈ Icc tmin tmax, HasDerivWithinAt α (f t (α t)) (Icc tmin tmax) t := by

label: IsPicardLindelof.exists_eq_forall_mem_Icc_hasDerivWithinAt₀
docstring: **Picard-Lindelöf (Cauchy-Lipschitz) theorem**, differential form.

    (hf : IsPicardLindelof f t₀ x₀ a 0 L K) :
    ∃ α : ℝ → E, α t₀ = x₀ ∧
      ∀ t ∈ Icc tmin tmax, HasDerivWithinAt α (f t (α t)) (Icc tmin tmax) t :=

label: IsPicardLindelof.exists_forall_mem_closedBall_eq_forall_mem_Icc_hasDerivWithinAt
docstring:
**Picard-Lindelöf (Cauchy-Lipschitz) theorem**, differential form. This version shows the
existence of a local flow.

label: IsPicardLindelof.exists_forall_mem_closedBall_eq_hasDerivWithinAt_lipschitzOnWith
docstring:
**Picard-Lindelöf (Cauchy-Lipschitz) theorem**, differential form. This version shows the
existence of a local flow and that it is Lipschitz continuous in the initial point.
code:
theorem exists_forall_mem_closedBall_eq_hasDerivWithinAt_lipschitzOnWith
    (hf : IsPicardLindelof f t₀ x₀ a r L K) :
    ∃ α : E → ℝ → E, (∀ x ∈ closedBall x₀ r, α x t₀ = x ∧
      ∀ t ∈ Icc tmin tmax, HasDerivWithinAt (α x) (f t (α x t)) (Icc tmin tmax) t) ∧
      ∃ L' : ℝ≥0, ∀ t ∈ Icc tmin tmax, LipschitzOnWith L' (α · t) (closedBall x₀ r) := by

label: LindemannWeierstrass.exp_polynomial_approx
docstring:
See equation (68), page 285 of [Jacobson, *Basic Algebra I, 4.12*][jacobson1974].

Given a polynomial `f` with integer coefficients, we can find a constant `c : ℝ` and for each prime
`p > |f₀|`, `nₚ : ℤ` and `gₚ : ℤ[X]` such that

* `p` does not divide `nₚ`
* `deg(gₚ) < p * deg(f
code:
theorem exp_polynomial_approx (f : ℤ[X]) (hf : f.eval 0 ≠ 0) :
    ∃ c,
      ∀ p > (eval 0 f).natAbs, p.Prime →
        ∃ n : ℤ, ¬ ↑p ∣ n ∧ ∃ gp : ℤ[X], gp.natDegree ≤ p * f.natDegree - 1 ∧
          ∀ {r : ℂ}, r ∈ f.aroots ℂ →
            ‖n • exp r - p • aeval r gp‖ ≤ c ^ p / (p - 1)! := by

      -(exp (-s) * p.sumIDeriv.eval s) + p.sumIDeriv.eval 0 := by

  | zero => pure 0
  | succ => Nat.succ

label: Ordnode.Bounded
docstring:
`Bounded t lo hi` says that every element `x ∈ t` is in the range `lo < x < hi`, and also this
property holds recursively in subtrees, making the full tree a BST. The bounds can be set to
`lo = ⊥` and `hi = ⊤` if we care only about the internal ordering constraints.
code:
def Bounded : Ordnode α → WithBot α → WithTop α → Prop
  | nil, some a, some b => a < b
  | nil, _, _ => True
  | node _ l x r, o₁, o₂ => Bounded l o₁ x ∧ Bounded r (↑x) o₂

def erase (x : α) : Ordnode α → Ordnode α
  | nil => nil
  | _t@(node _ l y r) =>

    | Ordering.lt => balanceR (erase x l) y r
    | Ordering.eq => glue l r
    | Ordering.gt => balanceL l y (erase x r)

label: Ordnode.eraseMin

label: Ordnode.find
docstring:
O(log n). Retrieve an element in the set that is equivalent to `x` in the order,
if it exists.

    find 1 {1, 2, 3} = some 1
    find 4 {1, 2, 3} = none

Using a preorder on `ℕ × ℕ` that only compares the first coordinate:

    find (1, 1) {(0, 1), (1, 2)} = some (1, 2)
    find
code:
def find (x : α) : Ordnode α → Option α
  | nil => none
  | node _ l y r =>
    match cmpLE x y with
    | Ordering.lt => find x l
    | Ordering.eq => some y
    | Ordering.gt => find x r

label: Ordnode.findGt
docstring:
O(log n). Get the smallest element in the tree that is `> x`.

findGt 3 {1, 2, 4} = some 4
findGt 4 {1, 2, 4} = none
code:
def findGt (x : α) : Ordnode α → Option α
  | nil => none
  | node _ l y r => if y ≤ x then findGt x r else some (findGtAux x l y)

label: Ordnode.findLt
docstring:
O(log n). Get the largest element in the tree that is `< x`.

findLt 2 {1, 2, 4} = some 1
findLt 3 {1, 2, 4} = some 2
findLt 0 {1, 2, 4} = none
code:
def findLt (x : α) : Ordnode α → Option α
  | nil => none
  | node _ l y r => if x ≤ y then findLt x l else some (findLtAux x r y)

label: Ordnode.glue
docstring:
**Internal use only**

O(log(m + n)). Concatenate two trees that are balanced and ordered with respect to each other.
code:
def glue : Ordnode α → Ordnode α → Ordnode α
  | nil, r => r
  | l@(node _ _ _ _), nil => l
  | l@(node sl ll lx lr), r@(node sr rl rx rr) =>
    if sl > sr then
      let (l', m) := splitMax' ll lx lr
      balanceR l' m r
    else
      let (m, r') := splitMin' rl rx rr
      balanceL l m r'

  | node sz l y r =>
    match cmpLE x y with
    | Ordering.lt => balanceL (Ordnode.insert x l) y r
    | Ordering.eq => node sz l x r
    | Ordering.gt => balanceR l y (Ordnode.insert x r)

  | zero : Nat.Partrec (pure 0)
  | succ : Nat.Partrec succ
  | left : Nat.Partrec ↑fun n : ℕ => n.unpair.1
  | right : Nat.Partrec ↑fun n : ℕ => n.unpair.2
  | pair {f g} : Nat.Partrec f → Nat.Partrec g → Nat.Partrec fun n => pair <$> f n <*> g n
  | comp {f g} : Nat.Partrec f → Nat.Partrec g → Nat.Partrec fun n => g n >>= f
  | prec {f g} : Nat.Partrec f → Nat.Partrec g → Nat.Partrec (unpaired fun a n =>
      n.rec (f a) fun y IH => do let i ← IH; g (pair a (pair y i)))

    Nat.Partrec fun a => rfind fun n => (fun m => m = 0) <$> f (pair a n)

label: RegularExpression
docstring:
This is the definition of regular expressions. The names used here is to mirror the definition
of a Kleene algebra (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kleene_algebra).
* `0` (`zero`) matches nothing
* `1` (`epsilon`) matches only the empty string
* `char a` matches only the string 'a'
code:
inductive RegularExpression (α : Type u) : Type u
  | zero : RegularExpression α
  | epsilon : RegularExpression α
  | char : α → RegularExpression α
  | plus : RegularExpression α → RegularExpression α → RegularExpression α
  | comp : RegularExpression α → RegularExpression α → RegularExpression α
  | star : RegularExpression α → RegularExpression α

label: RegularExpression.matches'

  | 0 => 0
  | 1 => 1
  | char a => {[a]}
  | P + Q => P.matches' + Q.matches'
  | P * Q => P.matches' * Q.matches'
  | star P => P.matches'∗

The fact that `SetRel` wasn't an `abbrev` confuses automation.

type to perform relation operations on. So we instead redefined it as

The order of a meromorphic function `f` at `z₀`, as an element of `ℤ ∪ {∞}`.

The order is defined to be `∞` if `f` is identically 0 on a neighbourhood of `z₀`, and otherwise the
unique `n` such that `f` can locally be written as `f z = (z - z₀) ^ n • g z`, where `g` is analytic

label: meromorphicOrderAt_eq_int_iff
docstring:
The order of a meromorphic function `f` at `z₀` equals an integer `n` iff `f` can locally be

`A₀ * B₀ + A₀ * B₁ + A₁ * B₀ - A₁ * B₁ ≤ 2^(3/2) • 1`.

We prove this by providing an explicit sum-of-squares decomposition
of the difference.
